alignments.note: Comparative adverb. No answering καί stands, so rules 82 and 100 are not in question and *as* is the whole of its English.
Rule 9: the supplied subject and the auxiliary ride with the finite verb, headed on the lexical verb.
Rule 43: recitative ὅτι, which the ASV marks by quotation rather than by a word. No English word answers to it, so it is not stretched onto the opening word of the quotation.
Rule 51's anarthrous clause: no Greek article stands, so the supplied indefinite determiner is a rule 7 helper on the noun.
Quantifying adjective, bare.
Rule 21's determinerless clause: the genitive's *of* stays with the bare noun, discontinuously across the adjective under rule 15.
Rule 9: the auxiliary and the subject pronoun ride with the finite verb, headed on the lexical verb rather than on the auxiliary.
Pronoun.
Rule 71: the improper preposition is rendered by a single English word, so no supplied frame is in question and that word is the head.
Rule 77: a relative pronoun expanded with a bare supplied antecedent heads on the relativizer, the pronoun's own lexeme being what *whom* spells.
Rule 9: the supplied subject rides with the finite verb.

Rule 105: the supplied appositional *even* is carried by an anarthrous noun, so it folds onto that noun as a rule 7 helper headed on the noun. Marking *even* added under rule 5 remains defensible; the precedent for the noun carrier is two units and one of them is hedged.

Corrected from *who*. θεοῦ stands expressed immediately before this article as the head noun the participle modifies, so rule 31's test is answered *has one*: `τῷ θεῷ τῷ κτίσαντι` → *God who created* is the identical shape and gives the relativizer to the participle, leaving the article realizing nothing. Rule 90 cannot bless the earlier reading, saying in terms that it blesses no unit in which a head noun is expressed, and rule 32's substantival split needs an article governing no head noun. That the noun is anarthrous does not matter: the ASV writes no determiner for the phrase, so the article has none to carry, and rule 23 decides it.

Corrected to take the supplied relativizer *who* along with its own verb, per rule 31's expressed-head-noun branch. Rule 66 then heads the unit on *giveth*, the word answering to the compound's verbal core, rather than on *life*, which answers to the incorporated ζῳο-.
Rule 21: the case preposition and *the* form one unit headed on the determiner.
Substantival adjective under its own article, which has taken the determiner.
Conjunction.
Coordinate participle rendered as a finite verb continuing the relative clause opened at s014; the ASV writes no second relativizer, so it keeps only its own verb.

Rule 22: the ASV writes a determiner and a supplied nominal in place of a pronoun, so the substantival article takes both words, headed on the nominal; the participle keeps the relativizer and its own verb.
Ordinary negative; no second negative word stands, so rules 41 and 59 are not in question.
Rule 32: the participle keeps the supplied relativizer and its own verb, the article having taken the determiner and the supplied nominal.
Comparative particle rendered by the two-word *as though*, headed on the word that glosses the lexeme.
Rule 74: the participial clause leaves its subject unexpressed, so the supplied pronoun rides with the participle, headed on its verb.

review_notes: Corrected s013/s014. The accepted alignment gave *who* to τοῦ as a substantival article under rules 32 and 90, but θεοῦ is expressed as the head noun the participle modifies. Rule 31 settles that configuration — `τῷ θεῷ τῷ κτίσαντι` → *God who created* leaves the article realizing nothing and makes *who* the participle's helper — and rule 90 excludes itself in terms from any unit in which a head noun is expressed. A reference comparison will report the unrepresented article as a disagreement, and that report is not a correction.

The anarthrous θεοῦ does not weaken this: rule 31's expressed-head-noun test asks whether a noun stands for the participle to modify, not whether that noun carries its own article, and the ASV writes no determiner for the phrase in any case.
s012 folds the supplied appositional *even* onto the anarthrous θεοῦ under rule 105; marking it added under rule 5 remains defensible.
s014 heads on *giveth* under rule 66's compound clause, the verbal element being the core and the incorporated ζῳο- the modifier.
